o1.biggest_strength: Every number traces back to the brief and checks out — the funnel table, the 4,300 errors versus 4,800 in-app abandoned carts, the 1,860 extra checkouts, the 560 orders and ₹34 lakh margin, and the ₹1,209 no-cost EMI guide all reconcile exactly, with a clean 4-week sample-size calculation.
o1.biggest_mistake: It makes orders per session the main metric for the mobile-only size test at a 12% detectable effect, so the most promising page fix sits on a 4-week read that will probably land flat, when add-to-cart with orders as guardrail would have answered it in two weeks.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use add-to-cart or checkout reach as the primary metric on the mobile-only, low-traffic tests with orders as a guardrail, and show the money each test is worth so the priority order has a rupee reason.

o2.biggest_strength: It reads the traffic honestly — add-to-cart as the primary metric where orders per session could never reach significance, orders as guardrail, an explicit warning that small real lifts will read flat — and names the right segment per test (desktop for EMI, in-app versus other mobile for the hero), with a half-to-all range on the checkout fix instead of a single ceiling.
o2.biggest_mistake: The per-test rupee projections are inconsistent: tests 2, 4 and 5 halve a relative effect that was computed on add-to-cart and then apply it to orders, giving an implausibly small ₹4.5 lakh for the size test, while test 1 does no halving at all.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Apply one stated money method across all five tests so each detectable effect translates into a rupee figure the owner can compare, and give a single all-device read for the hero-image test rather than an underpowered sub-segment.

reason: Both are accurate and usable, but Output 2 makes the technical call I care about most — add-to-cart as the read where orders are underpowered, with orders as guardrail — and its dated two-lane plan with a ship rule is what I'd actually run; Output 1's cleaner funnel diagnosis is undercut by a 4-week order-based read on the mobile size test that will likely come back flat.
